newsitem.title: USA: Rights group shows gay ad ABC refused to air.
newsitem.headline: Rights group shows gay ad ABC refused to air.

text.p: A gay rights group Tuesday previewed a 30-second commercial about job discrimination that it had hoped to air on the hit television show "Ellen," but ABC turned it down.

The spot, shown to the media in Boston and more than two dozen other cities, was created for the April 30 episode of "Ellen," when the lead character reveals she is a lesbian. ABC, owned by Walt Disney Co, would be the first network to have a show with an openly gay lead.

Human Rights Campaign, a national lesbian and gay lobbying group, said the advertisement is intended to raise awareness that it is legal in 41 states to fire employees solely because of their sexual orientation.

"The coming-out episode of 'Ellen' offers a unique opportunity for the HRC ad to shed light on this injustice. The commercial will increase public awareness of the need for all Americans to be included in basic legal protection from unfair discrimination on the job," Mary Breslauer, an HRC spokeswoman said.
HRC is lobbying Congress to pass the Employment Non-Discrimination Act, which would extend job protections to lesbians and gay men at the federal level.
ABC and 11 of its affiliates have refused to air the commercial, made by the Alexandria, Va.-based Semans Co., HRC said.
Only nine states include sexual orientation in their non-discrimination laws: California, Connecticut, Hawaii, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, Rhode Island, Vermont and Wisconsin.
The program's star, comedienne Ellen DeGeneres, announced in an interivew in the April 14 issue of Time magazine that she is a lesbian.
